items.name: Naval Tactics I: Ambush
items.description: An extended discussion of surprise at sea. One line, underlined and re-underlined by a former captain, cautions that a single well-timed volley is worth more than any number fired in haste.

items.name: Naval Tactics II: No Quarter
items.description: A privateer adaptation of Spanish Armada naval practice, favoring close action and decisive endings. The margin notes that ships sent down swiftly spare one’s crew the cost of prolonged prize-taking fights.

items.name: Naval Tactics III: Stretch the Supply
items.description: A long-standing naval practice emphasizing careful rationing and strict issue. Properly husbanded stores are said to keep a ship effective long after others are spent.

items.name: Naval Tactics V: Silence the Guns
items.description: A French naval doctrine favoring deliberate fire to disrupt enemy batteries. The margin adds, in a coarse and difficult hand: "Break the rhythm"

items.name: Naval Tactics IV: Shipshape
items.description: A well known Royal Navy doctrine holding that a well-kept ship preserves herself. Constant attention to order, repair, and routine is said to spare both hull and crew when battle finally comes.
